result.title: MAPLE: A Multi-Axis Parametric Knowledge Extraction Lens for LLM Evaluation
result.summary: LLMs absorb vast knowledge from training data, yet their inherently probabilistic nature offers no guarantee that this knowledge will surface in their outputs. To bridge this gap, Knowledge Extraction Enhancement (KEE) techniques such as activation steering, decoding adjustments, and prompting modify inference, potentially reinforcing existing predictions or surfacing less accessible answers. Yet their evaluations centered on aggregate accuracy, which obscures diverse effects by collapsing recovered failures and disrupted successes into a single score. We introduce MAPLE, a unified framework for characterizing how KEE techniques affect parametric knowledge extraction. Its diagnostic metrics disentangle these effects at the surface, probability, and beyond-sampling levels by measuring answer recovery and disruption, gold-token rank shifts on unrecovered failures, and recovery of answers missed by fixed-budget sampling. We evaluate six KEE techniques spanning decoding, activation steering, and prompting across three model families: OLMo2, Qwen2.5, and Llama3. Our analysis reveals distinct effects and trade-offs across techniques, highlighting the value of MAPLE for understanding and comparing KEE beyond aggregate accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MAPLE 诊断框架，在表层、概率与采样外三个层级用恢复/破坏指标，比较解码调整、激活引导与提示等六种知识提取增强技术在 OLMo2、Qwen2.5、Llama3 上的效果与权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 激活引导等推理期内部状态操控、以及区分「恢复失败样本」与「破坏成功样本」并考察超出固定采样预算的答案恢复，可能为核验 latent 推理干预的真实贡献与代价提供评价层面的借鉴线索，需人工进一步核查。
